ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This quarter’s missed volume is overwhelmingly a rank/position problem in non-brand: the three in-scope non-brand search campaigns are only at 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank, despite zero budget loss and only ~56–59% budget utilization. Auction data confirms you’re routinely below competitors (your avg top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors’ 73.2%), so incremental gains come from improving Ad Rank (bids + relevance/landing-page/intent alignment) and cutting waste, not from adding budget.
notable_patterns: Non-brand search visibility is extremely low due to rank: Auto IS 6% with 94% lost to rank (0% lost to budget), Home IS 5% with 95% lost to rank (0% budget), Life IS 7% with 93% lost to rank (0% budget) while budgets are only ~56–59% utilized.

Competitors dominate premium placement: your avg top-of-page rate is 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%, and your avg outranking share is only 9.1% while competitors appear above you 85.4% of the time (e.g., Nordkreuz position-above-rate 96.5%).

There’s meaningful spend tied to low-intent/low-quality queries: “insurance company phone number” QS 3.0 spent 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; “home insurance claims process” QS 4.0 spent 2,248.95 with cost/conv 244.45.

High-quality keywords still don’t win auctions: e.g., “auto insurance germany” QS 9.0 has only 5% impression share and 95% lost to rank; similar pattern for “home insurance cost” QS 8.5 (IS 5.5%, lost rank 94.5%).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is barely entering auctions (6% impression share) and is losing almost all eligible impressions to rank (94% lost rank, 0% lost budget) while only using 57.2% of budget. With ROAS 0.7 and evidence of low-intent leakage (e.g., job-related query conflicts and navigation-style terms), you need to improve Ad Rank on core commercial terms and cut waste before scaling.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Segment high-intent quote/comparison keywords into their own ad groups with tighter query controls; raise bids/targets specifically on QS 7.5–9.0 commercial terms while adding/expanding negatives for navigational/support/job intent; monitor top-of-page rate lift and marginal CPA/ROAS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Home is at 5% impression share with 95% lost to rank (0% budget loss) and the weakest economics (ROAS 0.75) alongside low average quality score (4.1). Spend is being pulled into service/claims intent (“home insurance claims process” QS 4.0, spend 2,248.95, cost/conv 244.45), depressing performance and likely dragging Ad Rank.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Rebuild around quote/price/comparison intent with dedicated landing pages and ad copy; isolate/limit claims/support intent via negatives and separate campaigns if needed; bid up only where query intent is clearly purchase-driven.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Life is also rank-choked (7% impression share; 93% lost to rank; 0% budget) and has very low average quality score (2.0), suggesting relevance/LP experience issues. Waste is evident on top-of-funnel education intent (“what is life insurance” QS 4.5, spend 858.99, cost/conv 613.56), which will not support the Ad Rank needed to win competitive placements.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Split educational queries from quote/comparison queries; overhaul landing page + ad relevance for life quote terms; concentrate bids on commercial intent terms and de-prioritize “what is…” content traffic unless explicitly valued.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix non-brand Ad Rank to win auctions on your best commercial keywords (not budget)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across the three non-brand search campaigns, search impression share is only 5–7% while 93–95% is lost to rank and 0% is lost to budget; budgets are only 56–59% utilized. Even strong keywords like “auto insurance germany” (QS 9.0) sit at 5% impression share with 95% lost to rank, while auction data shows you’re rarely in premium positions (top-of-page 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%; competitors above you 85.4%).
recommended_steps: Create a dedicated “Quote/Comparison (High intent)” structure (separate ad groups or a separate campaign per line) for terms like “car insurance quote”, “life insurance comparison”, “home insurance cost” and move them out of mixed-intent groups.

Increase bids/targets only on the high-intent cluster (starting with QS 7.5–9.0 terms currently at 5–7% IS) until top-of-page rate and impression share move materially; avoid broad, account-wide bid inflation.
Use auction-position monitoring by competitor (e.g., Nordkreuz position-above-rate 96.5%) to set an explicit goal for premium placement on your top converting terms before expanding coverage.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate on non-brand moving from 15.2% toward 30%+ while non-brand impression share climbs from 5–7% into the teens without ROAS deterioration.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop funding low-intent navigation/support queries that are driving extreme cost per conversion
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: You have high spend tied to weak-intent terms with very poor efficiency: “insurance company phone number” (QS 3.0) spent 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; “home insurance claims process” (QS 4.0) spent 2,248.95 with cost/conv 244.45; “what is life insurance” spent 858.99 with cost/conv 613.56. These terms also tend to depress relevance signals that feed Ad Rank.
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives for navigational/support patterns (e.g., phone number, customer service, claims process) in non-brand campaigns; if you need claims traffic, move it into a separate, tightly capped campaign with separate KPIs.
Tighten match coverage on quote/comparison ad groups (use more restrictive matching where needed) so the “quote” budget isn’t siphoned by informational/service queries.
Reallocate the saved spend into the high-intent quote/comparison ad groups where you’re currently losing 93–95% of impressions to rank.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on the worst offenders (starting with “insurance company phone number”) should drop sharply as impression share on quote/comparison terms increases.

recommendation_cards.title: Reduce competitor-brand zero-click leakage; ring-fence competitor terms and focus on conquesting only where it proves value
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: 48.3% of tracked search-term impressions are coming from zero-click competitor-brand terms, totaling 35,700 zero-click impressions (e.g., “bluewave insurance”, “harborline mutual”, “crestfield direct”). Only one competitor term is shown converting (“nordkreuz insurance quote”, 1.0 conversion), implying most competitor-brand exposure is low-yield and likely contributes to poor non-brand efficiency.
recommended_steps: Add competitor-brand negatives (or isolate them into a dedicated conquest campaign) so your core non-brand campaigns aren’t absorbing low-intent competitor navigation traffic.
If you keep conquesting, restrict to high-intent modifiers (e.g., ‘quote’, ‘comparison’) and set separate bids/targets and budgets based on proven CPA/ROAS tolerance.
Review search terms after the change to confirm competitor-brand impression share drops while quote/comparison coverage rises.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms moving down from 48.3% toward <15% while non-brand ROAS improves from ~0.7–0.89.

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve the negative keyword conflict that blocks measurable long-tail demand
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Two negative conflicts are blocking an estimated 3,810 impressions. The largest is negative “free” blocking “insurance quote calculator free” in Dynamic Search Ads - Long Tail (estimated 3,400 blocked impressions).
recommended_steps: Decide whether “free calculator” traffic is desired; if yes, replace the blanket “free” negative with more specific exclusions (e.g., ‘free policy’, ‘free phone number’) or add an exception via campaign/ad group negative scoping.
If you do not want ‘free’ traffic, remove the blocked keyword/theme from the campaign so reporting and optimization aren’t distorted by internally blocked intent.
Recheck the conflicts report weekly to ensure new negatives don’t block core quote/comparison keywords.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impressions and conversion rate on long-tail calculator/estimator queries after the conflict fix; ensure CPA stays within tolerance.

already_working: Brand Search - DE is not budget-limited (0% lost to budget; 52.2% budget utilization) and is producing strong efficiency (ROAS 4.7 on 34,552.32 spend with 1,122.8 conversions).

Ad creation fundamentals look solid: 80% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good out of 5), so the bigger limiter is auction position/rank rather than an account-wide ad-quality collapse.
Budget caps are not the bottleneck anywhere (every campaign shows 0% impression share lost to budget), so scaling should follow rank and traffic-quality fixes rather than budget increases first.

email_copy.subject: EUR 188,014 is blocked by rank — not budget
email_copy.hook: Your paid search account isn’t running out of budget — it’s being kept out of the auctions that matter. Non-brand visibility is being throttled by position, even when the intent (and query demand) is there to capture.
why_now_bullets: Market visibility is typically 21.0% impression share — your account is at 9.02%.
Germany insurance query demand is up 12.0% QoQ — but your account is losing 91.0% to rank (with 0.0% lost to budget).
Competitors are accelerating (+18.0% QoQ search spend) while your account is still capped by 91.0% lost to rank (and 0.0% lost to budget).
email_copy.stat_sub: Unlocked by fixing non-brand position + query quality (not raising budgets)
email_copy.impact_line: The biggest gap in your paid search account is non-brand Ad Rank: you’re entering too few eligible auctions, and when you do, you’re routinely pushed below competitors. That combination is what’s keeping an estimated EUR 188,014 out of reach this quarter — despite a daily budget of EUR 52,768 and no budget-based impression loss.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is where that missed value is concentrated across the three non-brand search campaigns in scope, so you can see exactly what to fix first.
email_copy.cards_intro: The fastest path here is simple: win premium placement on your best quote/comparison terms, then stop paying for the clicks that can’t convert — the cards below are prioritized in that order.
email_copy.working_intro: The good news: the foundation isn’t broken — what’s working today gives you a clean base to scale once rank and intent controls are tightened.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we close the visibility gap from 9.02% toward 21.0% impression share, the upside isn’t theoretical — it translates into 610980 additional impressions and 32802 additional clicks at today’s 5.37% click rate (and that’s the conservative version).
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this into a 14-day action plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with either “Tue 10:00” or “Thu 14:00” and I’ll send a tight plan to move rank first (without blanket bid inflation). If you’d rather keep it async, reply “Plan” and I’ll email the step-by-step checklist.
email_copy.ps: P.S. I’m not recommending a budget increase first — with 0.0% lost to budget, the quickest wins come from position and query-quality fixes that let your existing budget work harder.
